plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: A fragrant evergreen shrub with slender gray-green leaves and dense spikes of small tubular flowers. Widely cultivated in gardens and fields for its essential oil, and a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender fields in Provence reach peak bloom around late June to July, and the plant's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Hypericum perforatum
plants.description: A hardy perennial wildflower with bright yellow, five-petaled flowers dotted with tiny black glands. Found in meadows, roadsides, and open woodlands, and long used in herbal medicine.
plants.location: Native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa; naturalized in North America, Australia and elsewhere
plants.funFact: It is named for St. John the Baptist, whose feast day is June 24, because it typically blooms around the summer solstice and was traditionally gathered on St. John's Eve.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting streets with fallen blossoms. It is a spectacular sight in subtropical cities.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December), with some blooming in the Northern Hemisphere's early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in California, Florida, Mediterranean regions, and parts of Africa and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, and in Southern California, the jacaranda bloom is celebrated every year, and in some areas the falling flowers are said to bring good luck.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular, fragrant flowers rising on tall stalks. It thrives in warm, shallow ponds and wetlands.
plants.location: Native to Asia and Australia; cultivated in ponds across India, China, Japan, Vietnam, and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that repels water and dirt, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that inspired self-cleaning materials.
